author: difficulty46_author_b

source_artifacts.claim: Current level specifies a single movable nutrient sac, two any-weight flow pads, two hero-specific latches, separate upper/lower gates and exits, safe floor, and bubble lane.
Any pads count crate weight; hold gates depend on continuing occupancy while latch state persists.
Active pad effects open their linked barriers.
Bubble attacks produce temporary hero-specific effects and can be interrupted by the Isp upper latch.
Level 02 introduces hold-open-one-door then rescue-latch-both-door cooperation and bubble interruption.
Level 04 introduces a hero holding a route while the partner crosses to rescue.
Level 08 at position 8 teaches parking a nutrient sac on an any-weight hold pad, a direct lead-in but not proof of mastery.
Roster orders level_02, level_01, level_04, level_03, level_37, level_45, level_06, level_08 before level_34.

prior_knowledge.concept: Both matching exits and separate Isp/Pac controls define completion.

evidence.claim: The earliest room gives the both-exits goal and separate hero controls; exposure does not establish mastery.

prior_knowledge.concept: A hero can hold a pad to open a gate, then a rescue latch can preserve access for both.

evidence.claim: Level 02 has Isp hold a Pac door and Pac use RESCUE to open both doors; current room reuses hold/latch logic across two routes.

prior_knowledge.concept: A hero may sustain a bridge/route while the partner crosses to rescue.

evidence.claim: Level 04 explicitly cues Pac holding STEADY for Isp to reach RESCUE.

prior_knowledge.concept: A movable nutrient sac/crate can supply weight to an any-accepting hold pad and remain there while heroes move away.

evidence.claim: Level 08 hint and definition introduce the nutrient sac parked on ANY PARK; the current room transfers this from one valve to sequentially two flow routes.

prior_knowledge.concept: A bubble can temporarily affect movement; the screen has shown bubble cues in earlier rooms.

evidence.claim: Level 02 defines bubble interference and advises stepping clear; no player mastery is assumed.

mechanics.fact: A single light nutrient sac can activate either any-accepting FLOW hold pad; moving it to one flow opens the corresponding gate, and moving it away closes that route unless its hero latch has already activated.

evidence.claim: Both flow pads accept any weight and use hold activation; the level defines one light nutrient sac.
Crate weight contributes to any pad and nonlatched hold depends on occupancy.
The native route shows the lower flow active with the sac placed there.

mechanics.fact: Pac’s KEEP LOWER latch opens the lower gate and Isp’s exit lock; Isp’s KEEP UPPER latch opens the upper gate and Pac’s exit lock. Both latches are required for both heroes to finish.

evidence.claim: The hero-specific latch effects explicitly unlock the partner exits.
After both route seals are latched, all four barriers are open.

mechanics.fact: The mandatory upper and lower lanes are separated by full-height hero-specific gates; a broad safe_floor provides a recovery route below the route platforms.

evidence.claim: Upper shelf/lane, left staircase, gates and full-width safe floor are authored.

mechanics.fact: Gem’s bubble attack begins when UPPER FLOW is active and the Isp latch interrupts it; bubble effects can temporarily alter movement.

evidence.claim: Bubble targets upper lane, starts from upper_flow and is interrupted by Isp upper latch.
Bubble assigns FLOAT to Isp/STICKY to Pac and can be interrupted by the newly active bound pad.

mechanics.fact: No collectibles are authored in this level.

evidence.claim: Collectibles list is empty and exits are listed separately.

legal_routes.name: Park lower, latch Pac seal, move sac upper, latch Isp seal

steps.goal: Open the lower route by parking the sac on LOWER FLOW, then reach PAC LOWER latch.
steps.action: Move the sac right onto LOWER FLOW; use the lower safe-floor route and jump as needed to pass its gate and activate KEEP LOWER.
steps.expected_feedback: The sac supplies weight so LOWER FLOW opens pac_lower_gate after Pac moves away; KEEP LOWER latches lower access and Isp’s exit lock.
steps.observed_feedback: Replay snapshots show the sac on lower_flow and gate open; Pac later occupies pac_lower_latch, which latches and opens isp_exit_lock.

evidence.claim: Lower flow accepts any weight and opens Pac gate; Pac latch opens lower gate and Isp exit lock.
At frame 520 the lower flow is active while Pac is near it and sac sits on the lower-flow area.
At frame 570 Pac has jumped away; lower_flow remains active without a hero occupant while the sac overlaps it, and pac_lower_gate remains open.

steps.goal: Relocate the single sac to UPPER FLOW after the lower latch is secured.
steps.action: Leave the latched lower seal active and push the sac left to UPPER FLOW; this opens the upper gate for Isp.
steps.expected_feedback: The lower latch persists while the sac moves; upper_flow becomes active and opens isp_upper_gate.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1030 the sac has moved left onto upper_flow; the lower latch stays active and upper gate opens.

evidence.claim: Flow pads are hold-triggered; Pac lower latch permanently preserves lower route and unlocks Isp exit.
Frame 1030 shows upper_flow active with lower latch still latched and gates open for both route progressions.

steps.goal: Traverse the upper shelf/lane through the newly opened upper gate and reach KEEP UPPER.
steps.action: Use the left folds/stairs to regain the upper shelf, cross the upper lane, and occupy Isp-specific KEEP UPPER.
steps.expected_feedback: The upper latch persists, holds Isp’s route open and unlocks Pac’s exit lock.
steps.observed_feedback: The replay records Isp crossing to the upper lane and activating the latch at frame 1380; all four barriers are open.

evidence.claim: Hint, folds, upper lane, Isp latch effects, and upper/exit barriers define the route.
At frame 1380 Isp occupies latched upper seal; all four barriers are open.

steps.action: With both seals latched and both exit locks open, Isp continues along upper lane to blue and Pac along the lower floor to orange.
steps.expected_feedback: Each hero reaches its own exit; both seals remain active after their activating hero leaves.
steps.observed_feedback: Current-source ordinary-input replay reaches complete with both exits at frame 1810 and no deaths.

evidence.claim: Both latches open partner exit locks and exits are distinct.
Isp reaches upper exit while both seals remain latched.
At frame 1810 both matching exits are reached and status is complete.
Current-source replay of a retained ordinary-input route completes both exits in 1810 frames without deaths; this proves feasibility, not novice understanding.
The current-source replay first completes at frame 1810.

isp: Use the upper folds to reach the upper lane after Pac opens the route; activate KEEP UPPER to open both the upper route and Pac’s exit lock.
Reach the upper exit once both seals are latched.
pac: Move the nutrient sac onto LOWER FLOW and cross the lower route to KEEP LOWER.
Latch the lower seal, then return the sac to UPPER FLOW so Isp can cross; reach the lower exit after Isp has opened the partner lock.

common_mistakes.mistake: The sac is moved away from the first flow before that route’s hero-specific latch has activated.
common_mistakes.consequence: The hold-only flow gate closes and blocks that hero’s crossing.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return the sac to the corresponding flow, cross to its hero-specific KEEP latch, then move the sac to the second flow. Because the floor below is safe and the crate is movable, this requires repositioning rather than a reset; no intentional error route was run.

evidence.claim: Flow pads are held while weighted; the two latches are separate.
Non-latched pad state follows occupancy/weight.

common_mistakes.mistake: The sac is sent to UPPER FLOW before Pac has reached KEEP LOWER.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp’s gate may open, but Pac still lacks the lower gate and the lower latch needed to open Isp’s exit lock; the required dependency chain is incomplete.
common_mistakes.recovery: Move the sac to LOWER FLOW and have Pac latch KEEP LOWER, then return it to UPPER FLOW for Isp. The puzzle is reversible on safe_floor, though repeated pushing and climbing add traversal.

evidence.claim: Separate flows/latches and exit effects show why each route needs its own latch.
Crate can activate either pad by position.

common_mistakes.mistake: A hero falls from an upper platform during the climb or crossing.
common_mistakes.consequence: The room has a full-width safe floor and no hazards, so a fall does not kill; it returns the hero below the upper route.
common_mistakes.recovery: Use the left staircase folds to climb back; the explicit hint calls out this recovery after missing upstairs.

evidence.claim: Hint describes left-fold recovery; safe floor and staircase are defined, hazards are empty.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp is hit by Gem’s bubble while crossing the upper route.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp gets temporary FLOAT, which can change his trajectory or delay arrival at KEEP UPPER; there is no lethal hazard below and the route remains recoverable.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reposition and try the climb again; activate Isp’s latch to interrupt the bubble. The trace does not record this mistake, so recovery is source-based.

evidence.claim: Bubble affects upper lane and Isp latch interrupts it.
Bubble effect is temporary and the latch removes active projectiles.

reasoning.rationale: The route requires two linked uses of one movable resource: park the sac on lower flow, latch Pac’s route/partner lock, move the sac to upper flow, then latch Isp’s route/partner lock. Each seal changes which exit becomes available, so players must order the two routes and revisit the sac; this is several dependent causal steps, not just a single switch test.

evidence.claim: Hint and pad/barrier definitions specify the sac placement and reciprocal latch effects.
Pac latch secures lower flow and opens Isp exit lock.
Sac is moved to upper flow while lower latch remains active.
Isp latch opens all remaining gates.

cooperation.rationale: The two heroes must secure separate route seals, and each seal unlocks the partner’s exit. Pac’s lower latch must be established before he relocates the sac for Isp; Isp then supplies the upper latch that frees Pac. This is repeated mutual dependency across two stages, though it does not require simultaneous precision.

evidence.claim: Each hero-specific latch opens the other hero’s exit lock.
Pac latch opens Isp’s exit lock before Isp completes his route.
Isp latch provides the reciprocal unlock.

execution.rationale: The mandatory route requires several controlled pushes of the sac, Pac crossing the lower route to latch and returning to reposition it, and Isp climbing the left folds to the elevated upper lane. Both then traverse their own lanes to exits. The retained route completes without deaths, but its length and repeated route changes make the movement task sustained.

evidence.claim: Route includes movable sac, left staircase, long upper shelf and lower/upper exits.
Pac has returned to move the sac left onto upper_flow.
Isp has crossed the upper lane to his latch.
Current-source replay of a retained ordinary-input route completes both exits in 1810 frames without deaths; this proves feasibility, not novice understanding.

timing.rationale: The FLOW pads are occupancy-based holds, but there is no narrow window: the sac can remain on a pad, and each seal latches before the resource is moved. The upper bubble has a windup/cooldown and can temporarily affect Isp, adding mild timing attention without a chained required window.

evidence.claim: Flow pads hold while weighted; bubble windup and cooldown are readable and latch interrupts.
Hold/latch state follows weight and persistence, not a timer.

hazards.rationale: There are no authored hazards, and the room has a full-width safe floor below the elevated paths. Falling is a traversal setback rather than an established physical threat.

evidence.claim: Full-width safe floor and empty hazards are authored.

novelty.rationale: The crate-as-pad-weight solution was introduced in the immediately preceding level 08, while pad holds/latches and hero-specific rescue roles appeared earlier. This room recombines them into a single sac moved sequentially between two route valves and reciprocal exit locks, a new combination of familiar mechanics.

evidence.claim: Level 08 introduces parking a nutrient sac on a hold pad.
Earlier hold/rescue latch and route handoff lessons.
Current puzzle uses one sac to sequence two flow pads and two latches.

recovery_cost.rationale: Moving the sac to the wrong flow can be undone by pushing it back, and missed upper climbs return to the broad safe floor; the hint explicitly points to the left-fold recovery. No long irreversible sequence or lethal reset is defined.

evidence.claim: Hint gives upper-climb recovery; sac and pads are reversible; floor is safe.
The movable crate can be placed on a pad to restore the hold state.

solution_clarity.rationale: The captured start frame says “One nutrient sac. Two stubborn valves” and labels UPPER FLOW, LOWER FLOW, ISP KEEP UPPER STAYS ON, and PAC KEEP LOWER STAYS ON; a single sac sits between the flows. The locked first-encounter record identifies these cues but remains unsure where to place the sac and whether both valves are needed. They support moderate burden (2): roles and the one-sac/two-flow relationship are visible, while the sequential transfer and partner-exit effects remain unstated. The optional hint is not part of this estimate.

evidence.claim: Captured subtitle, sac, flow labels, and hero-specific KEEP labels suggest role structure but do not show the sequence.
Captured subtitle, sac, flow labels, and hero-specific KEEP labels suggest role structure but do not show the sequence.
The locked first-encounter rationale records which visible cues appeared clear and what causal question remained unresolved.

control_friction.rationale: There is no direct two-human keyboard reliability observation. A scripted ordinary-input route demonstrates feasibility only.

evidence.claim: Packet says no human novice played and idle captures do not test controls.
Current-source replay of a retained ordinary-input route completes both exits in 1810 frames without deaths; this proves feasibility, not novice understanding.

confidence_reason: The current source defines both flow pads, the movable sac, reciprocal latches, safe floor, and bubble. One current-source ordinary-input replay demonstrates the full two-stage route without deaths. It does not establish novice understanding, error rate, or two-human input reliability; mistakes/recovery are mostly source-inferred.

confirmed: The idle screen correctly signaled one sac, two routes, separate Isp/Pac stay-on roles, and a meaningful route-setup problem.
The initial hypothesis that route setup and hero positions were related was correct, but the actual relationship is more specific and sequential.
The earlier nutrient-sac/plate exposure was relevant; level 08’s source taught a persistent sac weight, though its observation packet alone did not establish learning.
missed_mechanics: The one sac must be moved from LOWER FLOW to UPPER FLOW in sequence; it is not placed on both simultaneously.
Pac latches KEEP LOWER, opening his route and Isp’s exit lock; Isp later latches KEEP UPPER, opening his route and Pac’s exit lock. Both latches are required for both-exit completion.
The flow pads are hold states supplied by the sac, while KEEP pads are persistent latches. Moving the sac before a latch can close the route.
Falls return to a safe full-width floor, and the hint names the left folds as upper-route recovery.
The bubble is tied to upper-flow activation and is interrupted by Isp’s upper latch; it is not a separate required route.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 3 because the actual route confirms several dependent actions and reciprocal locks rather than a single valve choice; causal difficulty is supported by specific route dependencies, not merely the room’s dramatic two-lane framing.

Cooperation rises from 2 to 3 because each hero’s route seal opens the partner’s exit, and Pac must secure the lower latch before moving the sac to enable Isp; this is repeated mutual dependency, not just parallel routes.

Execution rises from 2 to 3 because the mandatory path requires repeated sac pushes, Pac’s return to reposition the sac, and Isp’s left-fold climb plus upper-lane traversal; the elevated paths are not optional decorations.
Timing changes from unknown to 1: the gates are hold/latch driven without a narrow window, though the bubble windup can add mild movement timing attention on the upper path.
Hazards changes from unknown to 0 because source provides continuous safe_floor and no authored hazards; falls are recovery traversal rather than physical danger.
Novelty remains 2: a sac-on-pad was taught immediately before, and holds/latches were taught earlier, but using one sac sequentially for reciprocal two-lane exits is a new combination.
Recovery changes from unknown to 1 because sac placement is reversible and a missed upper climb has an explicit safe-floor/left-fold retry route.
Clarity remains 2 because visible cues identify each role, but the sequential sac transfer and reciprocal exit unlocks are not fully explained in the idle screen.
unresolved: No first-time pair has been observed choosing the lower-first sequence or understanding why the sac must later move to upper flow.
The ordinary-input replay shows feasibility but not how often players need the left-fold recovery or miss a latch.
Whether the upper bubble changes route accuracy for novices remains unknown; the available replay did not establish human response.

single_operator_note: One operator would switch between Pac’s lower route and Isp’s upper route, while also returning Pac to move the sac. The sequential dependency may make this attention-heavy; no one-operator play was observed and this does not affect two-human scores.
